chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام performed the obligatory tawaf as eight circuits. So he left seven, and built upon one, and added six to it. Then he performed the two rakʿahs behind the Maqam. Then he went out to al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. When he finished the saʿy between them, he returned and performed the two rakʿahs that he had left at the first Maqam.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of prayer associated with tawaf
key_terms.السَّعْيِ: the ritual walking between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two points between which saʿy is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other point of the saʿy rite
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: the Maqam of Ibrāhīm, behind which the tawaf prayer is performed
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةً: eight circuits, indicating an addition beyond the prescribed number
key_terms.سَبْعَةً: seven circuits, the valid required count for tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf required in the pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: What should be done if someone performs eight circuits in the obligatory tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who performs eight circuits in the obligatory tawaf instead of seven. It indicates treating one circuit as the start of a new tawaf, completing it to seven, then performing the prescribed prayers accordingly, including making up the missed two rakʿahs afterward.
